Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the quick turnaround on the RFP responses. The procurement/Risk team at Polar has a couple of follow-ups specific to TAM coverage and incident notification that we need to include in the final appendix:

- We need a continuity plan that shows who owns the on-call shifts (primary, secondary, escalation) and how ownership transfers across time zones.
- Please describe the notify chain for Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents (email/SMS/phone/Slack) and expected acknowledgement SLAs at each step.
- For regulated workloads, our auditors want a documented handover checklist for cross-shift transfer and an example of the 24x7 coverage roster.

Are you able to send a draft continuity/ownership plan and a short one-page notify-chain summary by end of day Wednesday 14 Oct? If you have a single spreadsheet we can insert into the RFP appendix that would be ideal.

Background: Polar expects vendor operational ownership to be explicit; the RFP scoring penalizes ambiguous handoffs.

Thanks,

Appreciate the clear asks. I attached a first-draft spreadsheet (TAM_Continuity_Proposal_v1.xlsx) and included a short notify-chain summary below. The spreadsheet includes:
- Primary / Secondary / Tertiary assignment per 8-hour shift (UTC and local conversions)
- Handover checklist (deliverables, outstanding tickets, current incidents)
- Pager escalation ladder with time-to-ack thresholds

Notify-chain (summary):
1) Customer on-call (if pre-configured integration) receives first alert via PagerDuty -> expected ack 15m
2) Redwood primary TAM receives SMS + email + Slack mention -> expected ack 10m
3) If no ack in 10m, Redwood secondary TAM receives SMS and a phone call -> expected ack 10m
4) If severity remains Sev-1 after 30m, Redwood escalation (Engineering on-call) is paged and the CS Manager is notified via phone.

Notes:
- We support SMS, phone, and email natively; Slack notifications require customer OAuth integration (we can include a recommended webhook config).
- Acknowledgement SLAs above are our operational target; contract SLA exhibits can be tightened per commit level.

Elena —

Attached is an updated plan tailored for Polar Bank (Polar_TAM_Continuity_20261012.xlsx). Key points and explicit language you can drop straight into the RFP appendix:

1) Coverage model (24x7):
- Primary TAM: Assigned for each 12-hour block; local-owner where feasible. Primary is responsible for incident triage, initial customer comms, and incident timeline updates.
- Secondary TAM: Peers who acknowledge within 5 minutes of a Sev-1 page and take over if Primary unresponsive or requires escalation.
- Engineering escalation: Tier-3 engineering on-call is paged after 20 minutes on unresolved Sev-1s (configurable per contract).

2) Handover / continuity checklist (required at shift change):
- Timestamped closure of open alerts OR clear owner assignment on each ticket (link to ticket)
- Summary of active incidents (severity, started-at, current mitigation steps)
- Confirmation of any in-flight model rollout/quantization jobs that might affect latency/cost
- Customer-facing update draft (if incident active)

3) Notify chain and acknowledgement SLAs (Sev-1):
- T+0: Alert sent to Redwood primary (SMS + email + Slack) — ack target 5 minutes.
- T+5: If no ack, secondary receives SMS + phone call — ack target 5 minutes.
- T+20: Escalation to Engineering on-call and CS Manager — phone + email.
- All notifications are logged to our incident timeline (immutable audit entry).

4) Evidence and auditability:
- Each notification creates an audit event preserved for 7 years (or per customer retention request).
- Handover checklists are stored in the customer runbook folder (link included in spreadsheet).

5) Integration options:
- We support PagerDuty, VictorOps, and direct SMS/phone. Slack and Teams require a one-time OAuth/webhook setup.

6) Contract options:
- Standard (shared tenancy): ack targets as above; 12-hour shift model recommended.
- Dedicated/Enterprise: we commit to 5-minute primary ack SLA in contract exhibit, daily on-call reports, and a named escalation contact list (names + cell numbers) for top-tier support.

Attachments included: Polar_TAM_Continuity_20261012.xlsx (spreadsheet) and Oncall_Notify_Shortlist.pdf (one-page notify chain).

If this looks good, we can finalize a short appendix paragraph and add the spreadsheet to the RFP package. Happy to jump on a 20-min call to walk through the roster and make any redlines.

Regards,
Aisha Rahman

Redwood Inference
